summary: The patch emits `source-read` during `resolve_references` (post-parse/write phase) with `doctree.astext()` and discards the return value, so it does not modify any source or feed anything back into the doctree — the include'd content is never actually replaced. It also violates the event contract (handlers expect a mutable list `[text]`, not a bare string), which would crash real `source-read` handlers like the one in the bug report.

issues.description: Fundamentally wrong approach: emit result is thrown away and the call happens at reference-resolution time on an already-parsed doctree via astext(). Nothing modifies the doctree, so the actual bug (include'd source not passed through source-read at read time) is not fixed.

Issue not resolved. source-read must run on raw source before parsing so edits reach the parsed tree; here it runs after parsing and the emitted string is unused, so include'd content still is not replaced in output.

Contract break: source-read handlers receive a list and mutate source[0] in place. Passing a plain str (doctree.astext()) means handlers doing `source[0] = result` raise TypeError, breaking existing extensions such as the reporter's.

Emitting source-read a second time (at resolve time) for every document risks double-invoking handlers with side effects and is invoked once per resolve pass, causing unexpected behavior for existing extensions.
